beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never commit it to source control and never print it to logs or expose it in error messages.
Create and reuse a single long-lived MongoClient instance (or equivalent pymongo client) per process, relying on its built-in connection pool; do not create a new client for every request.
Configure connection timeouts and pool size explicitly (e.g., serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, maxPoolSize) to fail fast and limit resource usage rather than using defaults.
Require TLS/SSL for all connections (tls=true) and verify server certificates (do not set tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true) to protect data in transit.

Use least-privilege credentials for app access (create a user with only the DB/collection privileges needed for seeding and runtime operations) and avoid using the account admin/master key for app runtime.
Rotate credentials regularly and store secrets in a managed secret store (Azure Key Vault or equivalent), referencing them at runtime rather than embedding them in configs.
Make seed operations idempotent: create indexes only if missing and upsert documents by stable id so the seed script can be re-run safely.

When creating a vector index, set the index engine and explicit vector dimension that match your embeddings (e.g., engine=DiskANN, cosmosSearch vector index with dimensions=1536) so runtime queries use the correct index.
Store embeddings as normalized (unit-length) float vectors if you plan to use cosine similarity and configure the index metric accordingly (e.g., 'metric': 'cosine').
Keep embedding vectors out of query result bodies when not needed—use projection to exclude the embedding field during retrieval to reduce bandwidth and JSON parsing cost.
Use prefiltering (metadata filters) to narrow candidate documents before the ANN step (e.g., filter by guideline type or language) so vector search operates on a reduced set and is faster/cheaper.

Design a partition key with high cardinality and even distribution (for example a synthetic 'pk' derived from document id or guideline id) to avoid hot partitions and to scale RU consumption predictably.
Provision throughput appropriately for vector-heavy workloads: use autoscale or higher RU/s for indexing and peak query times and monitor RU consumption to avoid 429s during seeding or batch upserts.
Implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter for retries on transient errors (network timeouts) and 429 (throttling); honor server 'Retry-After' when present.
Avoid returning raw guideline embeddings or internal index diagnostics via API; never expose vector data to clients—return only document ids, metadata and the generated structured advice.
Use explain() or the MCP server tools to inspect query plans for vector + filter queries and verify the request uses the intended cosmosSearch/ANN index rather than a collection scan.
Limit document size and avoid embedding huge blobs in a single document; keep each guideline section small (well under MongoDB's document limit) and reference external large assets if needed.
Use field-level encryption or client-side encryption for any protected health information (PHI) stored in documents, and ensure compliance with applicable health-data regulations.

When running tests or offline fallback logic, never use real API keys or production connection strings; allow a deterministic local embedding/LLM fallback via config flags and assert that production secrets are not present in CI artifacts.
Sanitize and validate user input to the triage endpoint (limit symptom text length, reject binary payloads, enforce character limits) to avoid injection-style queries or resource-exhaustion attacks.
Implement server-side and API rate-limits for the FastAPI /triage endpoint and require authentication (API key or OAuth token) to prevent abuse that could exhaust cluster throughput.

Keep separate collections/databases for test and production data (use database name sample_healthcare_06 for this sample), and ensure seed scripts target only the intended database to avoid accidental cross-database writes.

Log operational events (index creation, seed upserts, heavy queries, 429s) to a monitoring system but filter out secrets and PHI; correlate application logs with database metrics to troubleshoot performance issues.

For retrieval-augmented generation, include source attribution (document id and snippet) in the response and enforce prompt-engineered safety guardrails (always recommend professional consultation, never diagnose) server-side so they cannot be bypassed by the client.

When inserting/updating many embeddings, use batched upserts and monitor RU consumption; avoid single-document synchronous upserts in tight loops—use parallelism bounded by the connection pool and provisioned throughput.
